text:
**Short answer:** for most campers, a 250-500 Wh unit is the sweet spot. Jackery Explorer 300 Plus is the top pick for a weekend of phones, lights, a camera and a CPAP. If you need to run a fridge or cooler for several days, step up to something around 1,000 Wh or more.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 290 Wh)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus**, ~$249: 288 Wh LiFePO4, 8.3 lb, 300 W output. It was PowerStationGearLab's best overall for camping. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold on Amazon. [Buy link on the review page](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus**, ~$269-299: 286 Wh with a 600 W inverter, double the Jackery's. It expands to 572 Wh. [Same page](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300**, ~$199: 288 Wh with a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you get the standard model with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC". [Same page](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A**, ~$179: the budget pick, 268 Wh with a 600 W inverter. [Same page](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

OutdoorGearLab's lab tests scored the small Anker C300 (50) and Jackery Explorer 300 (52) fairly low overall, mostly because they're small. It still called the Jackery 300 its best buy for phones and laptops ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)).

## Multi-day trips, electric coolers, or a bigger group
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It has 2,042 Wh (1,710 Wh measured), 2,200 W output, and weighs 39 lb. It lists at $1,499 but was recently under $900 on Amazon. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: the best value pick, listed at $799 and recently under $530. It's compact but has a noisy fan and limited capacity. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Bluetti AC180**: 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, about 16 kg, with a 5-year warranty. It's $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF, which the retailer's page says it tested in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21. [Buy at Bluetti via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission, and the store's checkout has the final word on price. The AC180 can't be expanded with extra batteries. [Details](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**: WIRED's pick for camping at $1,079 on Amazon (list $1,199). It has 1,536 Wh, an IP65 rating, and weighs just under 40 lb. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## Tips
- Turn off a CPAP's humidifier. It can triple the draw, and without it a 288 Wh unit runs most CPAPs 3-5 nights ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)).
- Add up the watts of what you'll run and multiply by hours. A 150 W fridge for 10 hours is about 1,500 Wh ([Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html)).
- A foldable solar panel makes multi-day trips easier. Non-Jackery panels may need an adapter cable (~$25) for Jackery units.
- Black Friday and Cyber Monday are coming, so prices may drop in November ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)).

I can't browse live, so I don't have direct purchase links for the Jackery, EcoFlow, Anker and Bluetti EB3A units. The linked review pages carry the Amazon buttons, so check current prices there. If you tell me what you plan to power and for how many nights, I can narrow this to one pick.
